An under-eighteen driver charged after a crash causing serious injury or death may be denied license issuance or renewal even if alcohol was not involved. An unresolved court traffic citation can prevent license issuance for someone younger than eighteen.

lines.text: Serious crash can block minor licensing

narration.text: An under-eighteen driver charged after a crash causing serious injury or death may be denied license issuance or renewal even if alcohol was not involved. An unresolved court traffic citation can prevent license issuance for someone younger than eighteen. A driver younger than eighteen seeking court supervision for a traffic violation must appear with a parent or guardian. Court supervision for certain alcohol offenses can postpone a minor’s full graduated license for nine months. For a driver younger than twenty-one, at least two moving-violation convictions within twenty-four months lead to a license suspension of at least thirty days, with duration depending on offense seriousness.
